unit.title: Perform hair shaping on excessively curly hair

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What do barbers and stylists mean by "excessively curly" hair?
options: Hair that has been relaxed straight
Hair in very tight coils or kinks
Hair that is fine and very oily
Hair that falls flat with a loose wave

questions.stem: A client's coil stretches to about 5 cm but springs back to about 2 cm when you let go. Which word describes this?
options: Porosity
Density
Elasticity
Shrinkage

questions.stem: Why do you ask a client with coily hair how he wears it day to day (picked out, brushed down or twisted)?
options: The cut must suit how he styles it
It tells you how much to charge him
It shows you which guard needs oil
It proves that his scalp is healthy

questions.stem: During the consultation you see small, firm bumps and raised scars at the nape of a man's neck. What is the safe approach?
options: Shave the bumps off smoothly with a razor
Cut down to the skin to flatten the bumps
Avoid cutting close there and suggest a doctor
Squeeze the bumps, then apply aftershave

questions.stem: What causes razor bumps (ingrown hairs) in many clients with very curly hair?
options: Using too much shampoo on the scalp
Cutting the hair while it is still wet
Cut hairs curling back into the skin
Combing the hair with a wide-tooth comb

questions.stem: You find round, scaly patches with broken hairs on a boy's scalp. What should you do?
options: Cut around the patches with clean clippers
Do not cut; politely refer him to a doctor
Cut as normal and spray the clippers after
Rub oil on the patches and carry on

questions.stem: A client's coily hair is tangled and matted at the back. What should you do before cutting?
options: Detangle gently in small sections, ends first
Pull a fine-tooth comb through from the roots up
Cut the tangles out with the clippers
Wet it with hot water and brush it hard

questions.stem: Which comb is best for lifting and spreading very curly hair before a scissor-over-comb cut?
options: A fine-tooth tail comb
A metal lice comb
A small moustache comb
A wide-tooth comb or afro pick

questions.stem: What does the number on a clipper guard tell you?
options: How fast the motor runs
How long the hair is left
How sharp the blade is
How heavy the clipper is

questions.stem: On your clippers a higher guard number leaves the hair longer. A client wants it a little shorter than your #3. Which guard do you try next?
What does the lever (taper lever) on the side of many clippers do?
options: Switches the clipper on and off safely
Locks the guard onto the blade
Changes the speed of the motor
Opens or closes the blade a little

questions.stem: In a curly-hair cut, what job are T-blade trimmers mainly used for?
options: Taking bulk off the top
Cutting all of the hair on top to one length
Making a crisp outline at the hairline
Detangling the hair before the cut

questions.stem: Why should the moving (cutting) blade of clippers never stick out past the fixed blade?
options: It can cut or nick the client's skin
It makes the motor run more slowly
It leaves the hair a little longer
It stops the guard from fitting on

questions.stem: Your clippers are pulling the hair and getting hot. What is the most likely simple fix?
options: Press harder on the scalp
Clean and oil the blades
Spray water onto the blades
Switch to a higher guard number

questions.stem: Hair is stuck between the clipper teeth after a cut. What is the right order before the next client?
options: Disinfect, then brush off the hair
Oil, then wipe with a dry towel
Brush off the hair, then disinfect
Blow the hair off, then put it away

questions.stem: You nick a client while lining up and it bleeds a little. Which is the right action?
options: Use the shop's shared styptic pencil
Wipe the blood off quickly with the neck brush
Carry on and finish the line first
Gloves on, clean pad, single-use styptic

questions.stem: Your clippers have a cracked plug and a taped cord. What should you do?
options: Use them carefully until the salon closes tonight
Tape the plug as well and keep working
Wrap the cord in a towel to protect it
Stop using them, label them and report it

questions.stem: In a fade, where is the hair shortest?
options: Near the hairline
At the very top of the head
At the crown, where the whorl is
At the front, in the fringe area

questions.stem: What is the aim of blending in a fade?
options: To leave clear lines between the guards
To make the top and the sides exactly the same length
To hide the lines so the length changes smoothly
To move the hairline back a little further

questions.stem: Which way of moving the clippers usually gives a closer cut on very curly hair?
options: With the direction of growth
Against the direction of growth
Only across the head
Only with the guard taken off the blade

questions.stem: A client gets razor bumps after close cuts. How should you cut his beard line and nape?
options: With the grain, not too close to the skin
Against the grain, as close as you possibly can
With a razor, right down to bare skin
With blunt clippers, pressed in hard

questions.stem: What is a "line-up" (also called a shape-up or edge-up)?
options: A haircut that is one length all over
A row of clients waiting for a cut
A blend from long to short at the back
A sharp outline at the front, temples and nape

questions.stem: Why should a line-up follow the client's natural hairline?
options: So it takes less time to finish
So the hairline is not pushed back over time
So the trimmer blades stay sharp longer
So the client needs fewer visits to the barber each year

questions.stem: When lining up, why do you hold the skin slightly firm with your free hand?
options: To keep the client's head still
To stop the hair from shrinking
So the trimmer glides and does not catch
So the hair stands up straight for the scissors

questions.stem: A client wants a round afro. After picking it out, which outline should the finished shape follow?
options: A flat top with square corners
An even curve all round the head
Longer at the nape than on the top
Short sides with a long fringe

questions.stem: Which technique is often used to shape the outline of a picked-out afro neatly?
options: Scissors or clippers over a wide-tooth comb
Razor cutting on wet, tightly stretched hair
Thinning scissors used close to the scalp
Pulling sections tight and cutting at 0°

questions.stem: A woman with coily hair wants a short tapered cut. Why do you leave the top a little longer than she asks at first?
options: The top grows faster than the sides
Longer hair makes the cut quicker
You can cut more, but not add back
She will want to colour it later

questions.stem: A client with a silk press (blow-dried and flat-ironed hair) asks for a trim. What should you warn her about?
options: The trim will make her hair revert
The trim will make the press last longer
Her hair will grow back straight
After washing, it will curl up shorter

questions.stem: A client with a long, narrow face wants a short curly cut. Which usually suits him best?
options: Less height on top, some fullness at the sides
A tall high-top with very short sides
A bald fade with a long, high top
A narrow shape with extra height at the crown and top

questions.stem: What is a "high-top" style?
options: A shaved head with a full beard
An afro cut evenly all round
Twists that hang to the shoulders
Short sides with tall, flat hair on top

questions.stem: A barber rubs a twist sponge over a short curly cut. What does this do?
options: Straightens the hair for several days afterwards
Forms the hair into small coils or twists
Removes dandruff flakes from the scalp
Adds colour to the tips of the hair

questions.stem: Coily hair is often dry and fragile. Which product usually suits it to finish the cut?
options: A strong spray with alcohol
A clay that dries hard
A light leave-in
A lightener with bleach

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice suits a client who gets razor bumps?
options: Shave daily, against the grain, very close
Pick out ingrown hairs with a pin
Put strong alcohol aftershave on them
Avoid very close cuts; see a doctor if worse

questions.stem: How do you check that a fade sits at the same height on both sides?
options: Compare the fade lines from front and back
Feel only the top of the head
Ask the next client who is waiting to have a look
Look only at the side you did last

questions.stem: After shaping an afro you pick the top out again. Why?
options: To make it look longer in the photo
To add volume before the client pays
To find long hairs the shape missed
To dry the hair faster before styling

questions.stem: Why do you ask the client to bend his head forward when you cut the nape outline?
options: So he can watch the cut in the mirror
So the skin is flat for the line
So the hair at the crown stands up
So the cape does not slip off him

questions.stem: Short cut coily hair keeps falling into the client's collar. Which helps most to stop this?
options: Cutting faster at the nape
Wetting the hair well before you start cutting
Leaving the cape loose
A snug neck strip under the cape

questions.stem: Why do you use a fresh neck strip for each client?
options: Reuse can spread germs
It makes the cape easier to fasten
It keeps the clipper blades cool
It saves washing the cape so often

questions.stem: Cut hair has built up around your chair during a busy Saturday. What should you do?
options: Leave it until closing time
Sweep it up between clients
Push it under the station
Blow it away with the dryer

questions.stem: Jamaica's mains supply is 110 V or 220 V at 50 Hz. Why do you check the label on clippers or their charger?
options: To find the sizes of the guards
To see how long the blade lasts
To be sure it matches the supply
To see which oil the maker sells

questions.stem: Why do you write the guard numbers and lever setting on the client's record card?
options: So the price can go up next time
So the clipper maker's warranty stays valid
So another client can copy the cut
So the cut can be repeated next visit

questions.stem: Partway through a cut, you think a much shorter guard than agreed would look better. What should you do?
options: Check with the client first
Just do it, as hair grows back
Ask the receptionist instead
Do it, then tell him after

questions.stem: A client wants a part cut into his hair. What is the safe way to make it?
options: Cut it deep with the edge of a razor
Press closed scissors firmly against the scalp
Trimmers, used lightly along a combed line
Clippers with no guard, pressed in hard

questions.stem: Which part of a short curly cut do you usually finish last?
options: Taking the bulk off the top
The outline and detail at the hairline
Detangling the hair
The consultation

questions.stem: When is the cut finished and ready for the client to pay?
options: When he has seen the back and agreed the result
When the clippers have been switched off
When all of the bulk has been taken out
When the time for the service has run out

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the comb with long, wide-spaced teeth used to lift and shape an afro?
Razor bumps in the beard area have a medical name, often shortened to three letters. Give the three letters.
What is the name of the thick, raised scar that some clients form after a cut, bump or piercing?
What one-word name do barbers give to a cut where the sides go gradually from longer hair down to bare skin?
What is the name of the plastic attachment clipped onto clippers to leave the hair at a set length?
What do you put on clipper blades, as the maker says, to keep them running smoothly and cool?
What is the name of the holed sponge brush rubbed over short coily hair to form small twists?
What word describes how many hairs grow on each part of the scalp (thick or thin hair)?
Which fungal scalp infection shows round, scaly patches and broken hairs?
What is the name of the hair that grows down the sides of the face, in front of the ears?
Hair loss caused by tight braids or constant pulling is called traction what?
What is the flat area at each side of the forehead, where a line-up turns a corner, called?
Which single-use product, as a powder or liquid, is used to stop bleeding from a small nick?
On clippers where a higher number leaves more hair, which guard leaves the hair longer: #2 or #4? Write the number.
Into which closed container must a used razor blade go?

essays.stem: Describe the consultation you would carry out before a clipper cut on excessively curly hair, including what you would look for on the scalp and skin.
essays.modelAnswer: I would seat the client, gown him and talk before I cut. I would ask what style he wants, how short, and how he wears his hair each day (picked out, brushed or twisted), and show pictures to agree the look. I would ask about his last cut and the guard numbers used. I would look at the hair: the curl pattern, density, how much it shrinks and whether it is dry or tangled. Then I would check the scalp and skin, especially the nape and beard line, for cuts, sores, flaking, round scaly patches, head lice, razor bumps and keloid scars. If I find an infection or infestation I would not cut and would refer him politely to a doctor. If he gets razor bumps or keloids I would agree not to cut close there. I would write the agreed cut and guards on his record card.
markingPoints: Agrees the style, length and how the client wears his hair, using pictures
Looks at curl pattern, density, shrinkage and condition
Checks the scalp, nape and beard line for infection, lice, bumps and keloids
Does not cut, and refers, if there is an infection or infestation
Adjusts the plan for bumps or keloids and records the agreed cut

essays.stem: Explain what razor bumps and keloids are, why clients with very curly hair often get them, and how a barber should change the cut for these clients.
essays.modelAnswer: Razor bumps (PFB) are red or dark bumps that form when a cut hair curls back and grows into the skin, or grows sideways under it. Very curly hair grows in a tight curve, so a hair cut very close or against the grain easily turns back into the skin. A keloid is a thick, raised scar that grows bigger than the wound. Some people form keloids after small cuts or bumps, often at the nape. For these clients the barber should avoid cutting down to bare skin, cut with the grain rather than against it, use a guard or keep the trimmer lightly on the skin, and never squeeze or pick bumps. He should keep tools sharp and disinfected, avoid strong alcohol on the skin and not cut over a keloid. If bumps are infected or keloids are growing, the client should see a doctor.
markingPoints: Razor bumps: cut hairs curl back or grow into the skin
Keloid: a thick raised scar that grows past the wound
Very curly hair curls back easily, especially when cut close or against the grain
Changes: avoid bare skin, cut with the grain, light trimmer, no squeezing
Refer to a doctor for infected bumps or growing keloids

essays.stem: Describe the steps to cut a mid fade on short coily hair, from choosing the guards to blending the lines.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation I pick out the hair and agree the top length and where the fade should sit, about halfway up the sides. I take the bulk down on the top and sides with the longest guard agreed. Then I set the fade line with a shorter guard, cutting up to the agreed height all round the sides and back and checking it is level. Below that I use a shorter guard again, closer to the hairline, so there are bands that get shorter as they go down. Next I blend: I use the lever, flicking the clipper out of the hair at each line, and the guard between the two lengths, until no lines show. I can use clipper-over-comb to soften the top line. Finally I check both sides in the mirror, line up the edges with trimmers and remove loose hair.
markingPoints: Agrees the fade height and top length, and picks out the hair
Removes bulk with the longest guard first
Sets the fade line level, then works down with shorter guards
Blends each line with the lever, flicking out, or in-between guards
Checks balance on both sides and finishes with a line-up

essays.stem: Describe how to shape a rounded afro on dry, picked-out hair, and how you would check that it is balanced.
essays.modelAnswer: First I detangle the dry hair in sections, starting from the ends, and pick it out evenly all over with an afro pick so it stands at its full length and the true shape shows. I agree the size of the round shape with the client. I start at the nape and sides, using scissors or clippers over a wide-tooth comb to cut the outline into an even curve that follows the round of the head. I work up to the crown and top, taking off a little at a time, because I cannot put length back. I keep picking the hair out again to find any long hairs. To check balance I stand behind and in front of the client and compare both sides in the mirror, look at the shape from the side, and make sure the head is upright. I finish with a light line-up and moisturiser.
markingPoints: Detangles and picks out the dry hair evenly first
Agrees the size and shape with the client
Cuts the outline in an even curve with scissors or clippers over a comb
Takes off a little at a time and picks out again to find long hairs
Checks balance from front, back and sides with the head upright

essays.stem: Explain how to do a line-up neatly and safely with trimmers, and why the client's natural hairline should be kept.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the trimmers are clean, disinfected, oiled and that the blades are set so the moving blade does not stick out. I ask the client to keep still and tilt his head as needed. I comb the hair at the hairline into place and look at where the natural hairline is. Holding the skin slightly firm with my free hand, I use the corner of the trimmer lightly, starting at the centre of the front and working out to the temples, then the sideburns and around the ears, and lastly the nape with his head bent forward. I work in short strokes and check both sides match. I do not cut back into the natural hairline, because each line-up would push it further back and could make the hair look thin. If I nick the skin, I stop, glove up and use single-use styptic.
markingPoints: Trimmers clean, disinfected, oiled and blades set safely
Skin held firm; light, short strokes following the natural line
Works in order: front, temples, sideburns, ears, nape with head forward
Checks both sides match
Keeps the natural hairline so it is not pushed back

essays.stem: Explain how shrinkage affects cutting very curly hair, and compare cutting it dry and picked out with cutting it stretched or blown out.
essays.modelAnswer: Very curly hair shrinks a lot as it dries and springs back into coils, so it can look much shorter than its stretched length. If I cut it while it is wet or stretched straight and take off what looks like a little, it may end up much shorter than the client wanted once it dries and curls. Cutting it dry and picked out lets me see the real shape and length the client will wear every day, so the result is more accurate for afros, tapers and fades. Cutting hair that is blown out or pressed gives a smooth, even line while it stays straight, which suits clients who wear it pressed, but when it is washed it may curl up unevenly. For that reason I take off less, tell the client how it will look when it reverts, and agree the length before I cut.
markingPoints: Very curly hair shrinks as it dries and looks shorter
Cutting wet or stretched can leave it too short
Dry, picked-out cutting shows the real shape the client wears
Blown-out or pressed cutting gives a smooth line but may revert unevenly
Takes off less and explains the result to the client

essays.stem: Describe how you would clean, disinfect, oil and check clippers and trimmers between clients and at the end of the day.
essays.modelAnswer: Between clients I switch off the clippers and take off the guard. I brush all the hair out of the teeth and blades with a small brush. I then disinfect the blades and guards with a product made for clippers, used as the maker says, and leave it on for the contact time it gives. Hair must be removed first because disinfectant cannot work through it. I put a drop of oil on the blades and run them briefly so they stay cool and cut cleanly. I check that the moving blade does not stick out past the fixed blade. At the end of the day I clean more fully, take the blades off if the maker allows, and check the cord, plug and charger for damage. Any damaged tool is labelled, taken out of use and reported. I store tools dry and covered.
markingPoints: Switches off and removes hair from blades and guards first
Disinfects with a suitable product for the full contact time
Oils the blades as the maker says
Checks blade alignment and the cord, plug and charger
Takes damaged tools out of use, reports them and stores tools clean

essays.stem: Explain what you would do if you cut or nick a client's skin during a curly-hair cut, including how you would deal with the blood and the tools.
essays.modelAnswer: I would stop cutting at once and calmly tell the client what happened and say sorry. I would put on disposable gloves. I would press a clean, single-use pad on the cut until the bleeding stops, and use a single-use styptic powder or liquid on a disposable applicator if needed, never a shared styptic pencil. I would cover it with a small plaster if the client agrees. Anything with blood on it, such as the pad and gloves, goes into a closed bag or the clinical waste bin as the salon's rules say. The tool that caused the cut is cleaned, then disinfected with a product that works against blood-borne germs before it is used again. I would wash my hands, finish the cut carefully, avoid the area, and record the accident in the accident book. If the cut is deep, I would get first aid help.
markingPoints: Stops, tells the client and puts on gloves
Presses a clean pad; single-use styptic, never a shared pencil
Disposes of blood-stained items safely
Cleans then disinfects the tool before reuse and washes hands
Records it in the accident book and gets help for a deep cut

essays.stem: Describe how you would choose a suitable short cut for a client with very curly hair, taking into account face and head shape, hair density and lifestyle.
essays.modelAnswer: I would look at the face shape. A round face suits some height on top and shorter sides to make it look longer, while a long, narrow face suits less height and a little fullness at the sides. I would look at the head shape: flat areas at the crown or back can be balanced by leaving more length there, and bumps or scars may need a longer guard to cover them. Hair density matters too: thick, dense hair holds a high-top or round afro shape well, while thin areas may look patchy in a very short fade. I would ask about lifestyle: a client who works in the sun or has little time may want a low-maintenance cut, while a client who likes sharp edges must come back often for line-ups. I would show pictures, explain my advice and agree the final choice with him.
markingPoints: Face shape: height for round faces, side fullness for long faces
Head shape: balances flat areas and covers bumps or scars
Density: dense hair holds shape; thin areas look patchy cut short
Lifestyle and upkeep: how often he can return and how he styles it
Shows pictures, explains and agrees the choice

essays.stem: Explain the aftercare advice you would give a client with very curly hair after a short cut, including care of the scalp and the cut.
essays.modelAnswer: I would advise the client to keep the hair and scalp moisturised with a light moisturiser or leave-in conditioner, because coily hair dries out easily. He should use a soft brush, pick or sponge gently and not rake a fine comb through it. At night a satin or silk cap or pillowcase helps keep the shape and moisture. If he gets razor bumps, he should not shave very close or against the grain, should not pick or squeeze bumps, and should see a doctor if they become infected or keloids grow. He should protect the scalp from strong sun after a very short cut, for example with a hat. To keep the shape sharp he should book a line-up or fade in about two to three weeks, or as suits the style. I would note the guards and products used on his card.
markingPoints: Moisturise hair and scalp with suitable light products
Gentle brushing or picking, and a satin cap or pillowcase at night
Razor-bump care: no close shaving or picking; see a doctor if infected
Protect the scalp from the sun after a very short cut
Advises when to return, and records the details

practical1.title: Rounded afro shape on picked-out excessively curly hair
practical1.brief: As a group, shape a rounded afro on a training head with very curly (coily) hair, or on a group member or model who agrees, in the Centre's salon. First carry out and record the consultation, check the scalp, and agree the size of the shape. Detangle the dry hair in sections and pick it out evenly. Each member shapes one area while the assessor watches: nape, left side, right side, crown and top (in a group of four, one member also does the final balance check). Use scissors or clippers over a wide-tooth comb, taking off a little at a time, and pick out again to find long hairs. Finish with a light line-up with trimmers and a moisturiser. Every member checks the balance in the mirror and helps clean and disinfect the tools. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the consultation record to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the work area is clean.
materials: Training head with coily hair (or a model who agrees), with clamp
Cutting scissors and clippers with guards
Clipper disinfectant, blade oil and cleaning brush
photos: The consultation record card, filled in
The hair detangled and picked out before cutting
The finished shape from the front and from the back (no face unless the model agrees)
Tools cleaned, disinfected and oiled, and the area swept
checklist: Helped carry out the consultation and the scalp check
Detangled from the ends and picked out the hair evenly
Cut an even curve in their area with scissors or clippers over a comb
Took off a little at a time and picked out again to check
Checked balance from front, back and sides in the mirror
Used and handled scissors, clippers and trimmers safely
Cleaned, disinfected and oiled tools and swept up hair
safety: Check clippers, trimmers, cords and plugs before use; do not use damaged tools
Do not cut over cuts, sores, infections or keloids; tell the assessor
Carry and pass scissors closed; keep fingers clear of blades
Clean, then disinfect, tools between users; use fresh neck strips
Sweep up cut hair so no one slips

practical2.title: Mid fade with blended guard lines and a natural line-up
practical2.brief: As a group, cut a mid fade on short, very curly hair on a training head with coily hair, or on a group member or model who agrees. Agree the top length and the height of the fade, and record the guard numbers on the record card. Each member does one stage while the assessor watches: (1) remove bulk with the longest guard; (2) set a level fade line with a shorter guard; (3) cut the shorter band below it; (4) blend the lines with the lever, flicking out, or in-between guards; and (5) line up the front, temples, sideburns and nape with trimmers, keeping the natural hairline. In a group of four, one member does stages 4 and 5 with a partner. No cutting to bare skin with a razor in this task. Every member checks the fade is level on both sides, and helps clean and disinfect the tools. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the record card to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the work area is clean.
materials: Training head with short coily hair (or a model who agrees), with clamp
Clippers with a full set of guards
Wide-tooth comb, afro pick and soft brush
Clipper disinfectant, blade oil and cleaning brush
photos: The record card with the agreed guards and fade height
Bulk removed with the longest guard
The fade line set, from the side
The fade blended, from the side and back
The line-up at the front and temples
The finished cut from both sides, showing the fade level
checklist: Helped agree and record the guards and fade height
Checked and set up the clippers safely before use
Set or followed a level fade line
Blended the lines so no hard lines show
Lined up following the natural hairline with the skin held firm
Checked both sides match in the mirror
Cleaned, disinfected and oiled the tools and swept up hair
safety: Check that the moving blade does not stick out past the fixed blade
Do not cut close over razor bumps, sores or keloids
Keep hands dry and cords away from water and walkways
Use gloves and single-use styptic for any nick, and tell the assessor
Clean, then disinfect, clippers and trimmers between users
